notes:
Summary: enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity economics + deterministic latency. Customer is Sparrow Bridge Payments (global payments platform). Primary ask: predictable throughput for fraud-reranking pipeline and sub-200ms P95 chat/risk calls for short sequences (<=128 tokens).

Key technical constraints / asks:
- Throughput target: 25k inference TPS (embeddings hot path), 2k concurrent chat/risk sessions during peak (18:00-20:00 UTC).
- Tail latency target: P95 <= 180ms for reference model (LLaMA-2-70B quantized), P99 aim <= 350ms with fallback. Business requires written SLO in contract.
- Reserved GPU planning: want committed pool equivalent to 12xA100-80GB (or compatible) with 2x burst capacity. 60% baseline utilization expected.
- Autoscaling behavior: prefer headroom-based scale-up with warm pools (pre-warmed vms/gpu kernels) vs cold spin-ups. Must avoid cold starts > 3s for KV cache loads.
- Scale-down policy: cool-down 10m after sustained 30% below baseline to avoid flapping during diurnal traffic.
- Queueing behavior: need guaranteed queue priority for risk-scoring calls (high priority) and best-effort for background embeddings; separate queues or token-budget routing required.
- Warm pools: proposed warm pool size = 20% of committed capacity; customer requests SLA asserting warm pool effectiveness and metrics (time-to-warm, warm-hit-rate).
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to smaller quantized model when capacity constrained; must preserve fraud-detection precision above 98% relative to baseline — want eval hooks and rollback criteria.

Operational & contractual notes:
- They asked for explicit latency SLOs in the SLA (P95/P99, error budgets, credits) and burn-rate triggers for auto-rollover to burst capacity.
- PCI scoping: plan to keep tokenized PCI data externally; need audit logging and KMS integration. Security team will review Redwood Private option in parallel.
- Procurement expects 60-day negotiation window post-proposal; legal asked for sample SLA + SOC2 attestation.

Recent POC feedback (ops):
- Observed queuing spikes when the autoscaler uses reactive metrics only (CPU/GPU util). Need request-rate / queue-depth aware autoscaling.
- Cold-starts of new nodes introduced 1.2s additional latency for first requests due to kernel JIT and kv-cache warming; warm pools reduced that to ~120ms for warmed replicas during load tests.
- Batching behavior: dynamic batching improved throughput but increased max tail latency; they prefer a policy toggling aggressive batching for embeddings and conservative batching for latency-sensitive risk calls.

Quotes / paraphrases from stakeholders:
- "We need deterministic tail latency — customers lose money if a risk call times out." — Head of Risk (S. Patel).
- "If the warm pool works, we'll consider committed capacity + burst for peak season." — VP Infra (K. Alvarez).

Open action items and next steps:
- AE to deliver Dedicated sizing + MLF (monthly committed GPUs) proposal by 2026-03-16 (Maya).
- SE to provide autoscaler policy templates: queue-depth scaling, headroom thresholds, warm-pool sizing rationale (Arjun).
- Security to provide SOC2 report + sample PCI scoping checklist; schedule security review 2026-03-18 (Lena).
- Legal to provide sample SLA that includes P95/P99 and credits model; aim to start negotiations 2026-03-22.
